A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEP-based causal abstraction work. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations using brain-data covariances with simulated higher-level abstractions in Sections 6–7 and Appendix L.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical studies and adds unfiltered partial-prior results in Appendix L, Figure 7. The brain evaluations appear in Appendix M.

M1.justification: The objectives, constraints, and update procedures for LinSEPAL-ADMM, LinSEPAL-PG, and CLinSEPAL remain unchanged, including their appendix algorithms. Corrected row/column wording and additional explanations do not alter the procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain the same synthetic abstraction settings and prior-knowledge levels, plus the same brain applications mapping 45 regions to 14 macro regions or eight functional networks. The added figures document existing scenarios.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparisons still evaluate CLinSEPAL, LinSEPAL-ADMM, and LinSEPAL-PG; brain experiments remain CLinSEPAL-only. Figure 7 reports unfiltered scores for methods already evaluated, while newly discussed related methods are not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds a supplementary evaluation summary without Figure 4's 90% constructiveness reporting cutoff. Figure 7 also displays constructiveness scores rather than only the fraction of fully constructive maps. Original dimensions, optimization settings, and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 extends the partial-prior failure analysis by exposing outcomes excluded by the reporting threshold. It examines how small distributional misalignment can coexist with poor coefficient and support recovery for the nonsmooth methods.

E5.justification: Both specify 30 ground-truth abstractions per synthetic setting, with 50 initializations per abstraction for full priors and 30 for partial priors. V2 retains the boxplot reporting approach and adds no new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds unfiltered constructiveness, KL-divergence, Frobenius-distance, and F1 results, showing poor recovery by the nonsmooth methods despite low KL divergence. Existing Figures 3–4 and brain results are retained; v1 Figures 7–9 correspond to v2 Figures 8, 10, and 11.

T1.justification: V1's broad minimum/maximum eigenvalue remark becomes Theorem 4.3's stronger indexed interlacing condition, with a new proof in Appendix G. V2 also corrects the post-nonlinear mixing derivation in Appendix C.1 and revises Lemma D.2's measure-transport argument. These substantively strengthen and revise the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SEP, the categorical framework, observational abstraction learning, three optimization methods, and synthetic/brain validation. The additional theory and reporting do not redefine those core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds an ellipsoid interpretation of the spectral restrictions and explains why learning remains nonconvex even with full structural priors and paired observations (Remark 1). Figure 7's discussion additionally emphasizes that low KL divergence need not indicate a good abstraction.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, explicitly describes generating missing synthetic priors by setting selected rows of B to one, and shows the brain prior masks in Figure 9. These improve documentation of existing experiments; solver choices and Appendix K hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion gains focused distinctions from IIT-based mechanistic interpretability and causal representation learning, plus connections to causal semantic communications. New citations support these comparisons and the spectral theorem; merged supplementary references and publication updates are not new works.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized explanations and wording corrections while retaining most prose and the main section sequence. It consolidates the supplementary bibliography, inserts a synthetic-results appendix, relabels the brain appendix from L to M, and updates affiliations and publication information.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 7's unfiltered comparison panels and Figure 9's prior-mask heatmaps, corrects Figure 5's left/right caption, and clarifies Figure 4's legend reference. Existing plots and the overall layout style are preserved despite reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The stronger spectral condition and proof improve theoretical support, while Appendix C.1 repairs an invalid nonlinear expansion. Unfiltered results make failures easier to assess, and the code link and explicit prior masks improve reproducibility information. These are useful gains in rigor and transparency within an otherwise largely unchanged study.
